title: Evidence & Measurement
learningOutcome: Measure cultivation systems with defined variables, calibrated instruments, representative sampling, baselines and controls; preserve uncertainty and context; and connect observations to decisions without confusing precision, correlation or one dramatic image with proof.
evidenceBoundary: Measurement quality depends on the complete chain: question, instrument, calibration, placement, timing, sampling, metadata and interpretation. More decimal places or more data points do not repair a biased method.

sourceRefs.citation: Guidelines for measuring and reporting environmental parameters for experiments in greenhouses. 2015.
sourceRefs.supports: Sensor selection, accuracy, precision, calibration, placement, units and reporting of light, temperature, gases, water and nutrient parameters.

sourceRefs.citation: Controlled-environment cannabis research across lighting, nutrition, water and post-harvest studies.
sourceRefs.supports: Cannabis responses are genotype-, stage-, environment- and method-dependent, making context and repeatable measurement essential.

sourceRefs.citation: Core experimental-design principles: replication, randomization, controls, predefined outcomes and uncertainty reporting.
sourceRefs.supports: Separating treatment effects from position, time, measurement and sampling bias.

sourceRefs.supports: Calibration and sensor placement are part of data quality, not optional housekeeping.

chapters.title: From Question to Measurement Model
chapters.objective: Turn cultivation questions into variables, units and comparison plans before collecting numbers.

lessons.title: Start with the decision, not the sensor
lessons.summary: A measurement is useful when it answers a defined question such as whether light is uniform, roots are drying predictably or an intervention changed disease pressure.
lessons.cultivation: Write the decision and the variable that would change it before buying or deploying instrumentation.
lessons.observe: Record the question, variable, unit, sampling location and action that different results would trigger.

lessons.title: Operational definitions make observations repeatable
lessons.summary: Terms like dry, high light, healthy roots or vigorous become useful data only after the observation or measurement rule is defined.
lessons.cultivation: Replace vague adjectives with measurable criteria whenever the information will guide comparison or breeding.
lessons.observe: Write the exact scoring rubric, unit or visual rule before data collection.

lessons.title: Independent and response variables must be separated
lessons.summary: The factor intentionally changed is different from the outcome measured, while uncontrolled co-varying factors can create confounding.
lessons.cultivation: When testing a change, keep other major factors stable or record them explicitly.
lessons.observe: List treatment, outcomes and plausible confounders before the run.

lessons.title: One number rarely represents a dynamic crop
lessons.summary: Plants experience cycles, gradients and developmental change; a point reading can miss night transitions, irrigation events or canopy hotspots.
lessons.cultivation: Choose measurement frequency and locations that match how quickly the variable changes.
lessons.observe: Record timestamp, plant stage, equipment state and position for every critical measurement.

chapters.title: Accuracy, Precision, Resolution & Calibration
chapters.objective: Understand instrument quality and calibration well enough to know whether a reported change is biological or measurement error.

lessons.title: Accuracy and precision answer different questions
lessons.summary: Accuracy describes closeness to the true value while precision describes repeatability among measurements; an instrument can be precise yet consistently biased.
lessons.cultivation: Do not interpret repeatable readings as proof they are correct without calibration or reference checks.
lessons.observe: Record reference standard, observed deviation and repeated readings.

lessons.title: Resolution does not equal accuracy
lessons.summary: A display showing two decimal places may still have much larger uncertainty, so extra digits can create false confidence.
lessons.cultivation: Report values at a precision supported by the instrument and method instead of preserving meaningless decimals.
lessons.observe: Keep manufacturer accuracy specification and calibration result with the instrument record.

lessons.title: Calibration is part of the measurement chain
lessons.summary: pH, EC, humidity, CO2 and other sensors drift or respond to contamination and aging; calibration connects instrument output to a known reference.
lessons.cultivation: Use appropriate standards and intervals from validated methods or manufacturer guidance, especially before high-consequence comparisons.
lessons.observe: Log calibration date, standards, pre/post deviation, maintenance and operator.

lessons.title: Cross-checks can reveal hidden sensor failure
lessons.summary: Comparing a field sensor to a maintained reference or overlapping sensors can expose drift, placement errors or damaged probes.
lessons.cultivation: Use periodic comparison rather than waiting for crop symptoms to reveal a bad sensor.
lessons.observe: Record paired readings under the same location and conditions and investigate persistent offsets.

chapters.title: Sensor Placement & Spatial Sampling
chapters.objective: Measure where the plant experiences the environment and use spatial sampling to expose gradients hidden by room averages.

lessons.title: Sensor placement changes the value measured
lessons.summary: Temperature, humidity, PPFD, CO2 and airflow vary with height, canopy density, equipment and distance from sources, so location is part of the measurement definition.
lessons.cultivation: Define height and position relative to canopy and equipment, and keep them consistent when comparing runs.
lessons.observe: Record coordinates or zone, height, canopy stage and nearby sources or obstructions.

lessons.title: Canopy measurements should follow a reproducible grid
lessons.summary: A grid reveals hotspots and low zones that an average can hide, especially for PPFD, temperature or canopy microclimate.
lessons.cultivation: Reuse the same grid after fixture, canopy or HVAC changes so differences can be attributed to the change.
lessons.observe: Store raw grid values, not only the average or heatmap.

lessons.title: Random sampling reduces selection bias
lessons.summary: Choosing only the most damaged, healthiest or easiest-to-reach leaves can exaggerate or hide a population pattern.
lessons.cultivation: Combine fixed sentinel locations with randomized sampling when the goal is crop-level inference.
lessons.observe: Record how plants or leaves were chosen and the number sampled.

lessons.title: Sampling unit determines what a count means
lessons.summary: Five mites per leaf, five mites per plant and five mites per trap are different metrics; comparisons require the same unit and observation effort.
lessons.cultivation: Define the denominator before counting pests, lesions, roots or flowers.
lessons.observe: Store both count and sampling effort so rates can be reconstructed.

knowledgeChecks: Why must sensor position be documented?

chapters.title: Baselines, Controls & Change Isolation
chapters.objective: Use baselines and controls to distinguish normal variation from the effect of a cultivation change.

lessons.title: A baseline describes the system before intervention
lessons.summary: Without pre-change data, it is difficult to know whether an apparent improvement was already underway or falls within normal variation.
lessons.cultivation: Collect enough stable pre-change observations to characterize the metric before altering the system.
lessons.observe: Record baseline window, conditions and variability, not only one starting value.

lessons.title: Controls provide a comparison that did not receive the treatment
lessons.summary: A contemporaneous control helps separate treatment effects from time, plant age, weather or room-wide changes.
lessons.cultivation: When practical, retain comparable untreated plants or zones rather than relying only on last cycle.
lessons.observe: Record how control and treatment units were assigned and any differences between them.

lessons.title: Change one major variable when learning causality
lessons.summary: Stacking nutrient, light, irrigation and environment changes together can improve the crop yet destroy the ability to know which change mattered.
lessons.cultivation: Separate changes when the goal is learning; if emergency correction requires multiple actions, document that causal attribution is limited.
lessons.observe: Maintain a timestamped change log with reason and expected effect.

lessons.title: Position effects can masquerade as treatment effects
lessons.summary: Bench edge, airflow, irrigation pressure, fixture overlap and worker access can systematically differ across positions.
lessons.cultivation: Randomize or block treatment positions when testing methods across a nonuniform space.
lessons.observe: Map treatment assignments and compare environmental conditions by position.

knowledgeChecks: Why is one pre-change reading a weak baseline?

chapters.title: Time Series, Events & Derived Metrics
chapters.objective: Interpret dynamic variables by aligning measurements with plant events and understanding how derived metrics are calculated.

lessons.title: Timestamps turn measurements into process data
lessons.summary: Irrigation, lights-on, lights-off, HVAC cycling and training events change the meaning of temperature, RH, EC and water-content readings.
lessons.cultivation: Synchronize logs so environmental and root-zone responses can be compared to the event that caused them.
lessons.observe: Store local timestamp or time zone, device clock checks and event times.

lessons.title: Averages can hide damaging excursions
lessons.summary: A daily mean temperature or RH can look acceptable while brief extremes or repeated transitions create stress or condensation risk.
lessons.cultivation: Review maxima, minima, duration and timing for variables where excursions matter.
lessons.observe: Preserve raw or suitably frequent time-series data instead of only daily summaries.

lessons.title: Derived metrics inherit input error
lessons.summary: VPD, DLI, dryback percentage and uniformity metrics are calculated from measured inputs; sensor error or inconsistent definitions propagate into the result.
lessons.cultivation: Keep the raw inputs and calculation method alongside the derived value.
lessons.observe: Record formula, units, sampling interval and sensor source for each derived metric.

lessons.title: Use the right statistic for the decision
lessons.summary: Mean, median, range, coefficient of variation and percentile answer different questions about central tendency and spread.
lessons.cultivation: Choose summaries that reveal the risk relevant to the decision rather than defaulting to an average.
lessons.observe: Keep raw observations so alternative summaries can be calculated later.

knowledgeChecks: Why should measurements be aligned to events?

chapters.title: Imaging, Observation & Scoring
chapters.objective: Make visual evidence comparable by controlling capture conditions, identity, scale and interpretation.

lessons.title: Images need identity and scale
lessons.summary: A close-up without plant ID, tissue location or size reference can look compelling but cannot reliably support trend or comparison.
lessons.cultivation: Capture an overview plus close-up and include a reference when size matters.
lessons.observe: Store plant ID, date, tissue or site, camera or magnification and scale information.

lessons.title: Lighting and white balance can change apparent symptoms
lessons.summary: Leaf color and lesion contrast shift with spectrum, exposure and phone processing, so uncontrolled images can invent or hide visual differences.
lessons.cultivation: Use consistent neutral lighting and avoid filters when images will be compared diagnostically.
lessons.observe: Record light source and preserve unedited originals.

lessons.title: Separate observation from interpretation
lessons.summary: Yellowing between veins is an observation; naming a nutrient deficiency is an interpretation that requires supporting evidence.
lessons.cultivation: Write visible features first and hypotheses second so later evidence can revise the diagnosis without rewriting history.
lessons.observe: Use separate fields for observed signs, candidate causes and confidence.

lessons.title: Ordinal scores need anchors
lessons.summary: A 1–5 vigor or disease score becomes more reliable when each number has a written visual or quantitative definition.
lessons.cultivation: Train scorers on example anchors and periodically compare scoring among people.
lessons.observe: Store scorer, rubric version and notes for borderline cases.

knowledgeChecks: What metadata make an image useful evidence?

chapters.title: Uncertainty, Replication & Statistical Thinking
chapters.objective: Interpret variation and repeated observations without turning small samples or correlations into certainty.

lessons.title: Biological systems contain real variation
lessons.summary: Two genetically similar plants can differ because of microenvironment, developmental timing and stochastic biology; variation is data rather than automatic error.
lessons.cultivation: Report spread and sample size alongside averages when comparing groups.
lessons.observe: Keep individual-plant data instead of only group means.

lessons.title: Replication estimates repeatability
lessons.summary: Independent plants, batches or runs help reveal whether an effect is robust or depended on one unit or one cycle.
lessons.cultivation: Match the level of replication to the claim; multiple leaves on one plant are not multiple independent plants.
lessons.observe: Record the experimental unit and distinguish technical from biological replicates.

lessons.title: Correlation does not identify cause by itself
lessons.summary: Two variables can move together because one affects the other, both respond to a third factor or the relationship is coincidental.
lessons.cultivation: Use controlled changes, temporal order and mechanism when moving from association to causal claims.
lessons.observe: Preserve candidate confounders and avoid causal wording in observational summaries.

lessons.title: Uncertainty should change decision confidence
lessons.summary: Measurement error, small sample size, inconsistent observations or conflicting evidence should reduce confidence rather than be hidden.
lessons.cultivation: Label low-confidence diagnoses and prioritize measurements that would discriminate among alternatives.
lessons.observe: Record confidence and the next observation or test that could change the conclusion.

knowledgeChecks: Why is plant-to-plant variation not automatically bad data?

chapters.title: Records, Reproducibility & Decision Learning
chapters.objective: Build cultivation records that allow a future grower to reconstruct what happened, compare cycles and learn from interventions.

lessons.title: A useful record can reconstruct the event
lessons.summary: Numbers without units, times, locations or equipment state are difficult to interpret later; reproducible records include enough context for another person to repeat the measurement.
lessons.cultivation: Define required fields for each measurement type rather than relying on free-form notes.
lessons.observe: Audit whether a later reviewer can identify who, what, where, when, how and why.

lessons.title: Stable IDs connect observations across systems
lessons.summary: Plant, room, sensor, seed-lot and image IDs allow measurements, genetics and interventions to be joined without depending on names that may change.
lessons.cultivation: Assign IDs at intake or creation and keep human-readable names as separate fields.
lessons.observe: Check that images, measurements and intervention logs resolve to the same plant or zone IDs.

lessons.title: Version methods when procedures change
lessons.summary: Changing a calibration method, sampling grid or scoring rubric can shift data even if the crop is identical.
lessons.cultivation: Version SOPs and record which version generated each dataset.
lessons.observe: Maintain effective dates and change notes for measurement procedures.

lessons.title: Close the loop from data to decision to outcome
lessons.summary: The highest-value record connects observation, interpretation, action and later result so the system learns which decisions were effective.
lessons.cultivation: For important interventions, write the expected result and follow-up time before acting.
lessons.observe: Review whether the expected outcome occurred and update the working model rather than only archiving data.
